ai.literal: He who knows the intention by looking, without speaking, is at all times an ornament to the world of unchanging water.
ai.translation: One who can read another's mind simply by looking, without a word being spoken, is an ornament at all times to this world surrounded by the eternal sea.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் வாயால் சொல்லாமலேயே அவருடைய முகத்தையும் கண்ணையும் நோக்கி அவரது குறிப்பை அறிந்துகொள்பவர், வற்றாத கடல் நீரால் சூழப்பட்ட இந்த உலகத்திற்கு எக்காலத்திலும் ஒரு சிறந்த அணிகலன் ஆவார்.
ai.explanation: This couplet praises the rare and valuable skill of reading another person's mind or intentions without them having to express it in words. The poet states that a person who possesses this intuitive ability is a true ornament to the entire world. The world is described as being surrounded by 'unchanging water', referring to the vast, eternal ocean. By comparing such an insightful person to a precious jewel, the couplet highlights how highly society values those who can perceive unspoken thoughts and feelings through simple observation.

ai.literal: Without doubting, that which is in the mind, him who perceives, with god, as equal, considering.
ai.translation: One who can perceive what is in another's mind without any doubt should be considered equal to a god.
ai.modern: மனதில் உள்ளதைச் சந்தேகமின்றி உணர்ந்து கொள்பவனைத் தெய்வத்திற்குச் சமமாகக் கருத வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet extols the rare and powerful ability to read the unspoken thoughts of others. The poet states that someone who can look at another person and instantly, without any hesitation or doubt, understand what is hidden in their mind (akattatu) possesses a perception that is beyond ordinary human limits. Such an individual is so insightful that they should be treated as equal to a divine being (teyvam). The word 'aiyappaṭāatu' uses a poetic lengthening to emphasize the absolute certainty of this perception.

ai.literal: By a mere sign, the inner intention of another those who understand, among one's own limbs whatever even giving, one should secure them.
ai.translation: One should secure the companionship of those who can read another's mind by a mere sign, even if it means giving away any of one's own limbs to obtain them.
ai.modern: ஒரு குறிப்பைக் கொண்டே மற்றவரின் மனக்குறிப்பை உணர்ந்து கொள்ளும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களை, நம் உடலின் உறுப்புகளில் எதனைக் கொடுத்தாவது துணையாகப் பெற்றுக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the extraordinary value of advisors or companions who possess the intuitive ability to read thoughts. The phrase 'குறிப்பின் குறிப்பு உணர்வாரை' refers to those rare individuals who can perceive another person's hidden intentions ('குறிப்பு') simply by observing a subtle outward sign ('குறிப்பின்') like a facial expression or gesture. The poet uses a powerful hyperbole, stating that one should secure ('கொளல்') such people at any cost. Even if one has to part with any of one's own bodily organs ('உறுப்பினுள் யாது கொடுத்தும்'), the trade is worth it because an insightful companion is far more valuable than a physical limb.

ai.literal: With those who grasp that which is intended without speaking, the others are alike in limbs indeed, but different.
ai.translation: Compared to those who can grasp another's thoughts without them being spoken, other people are similar only in their physical limbs, but are entirely different in their inner capacity.
ai.modern: மனதில் நினைத்ததை வாயால் சொல்லாமலேயே புரிந்து கொள்பவர்களோடு ஒப்பிடும்போது, மற்றவர்கள் உடலமைப்பால் மட்டுமே அவர்களைப் போன்றவர்கள்; அறிவால் வேறுபட்டவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet praises the rare and valuable skill of reading another person's mind or intentions without needing explicit words. The poet compares those who possess this sharp perception with ordinary people who lack it. He states that although ordinary people look physically identical to these perceptive individuals, having the same human limbs (uruppu), they are fundamentally different (veru) in their mental capacity. The physical resemblance is merely superficial, while the true distinction lies in the power of the mind.

ai.literal: If [they] do not understand the intention [of another] by [their] sign, among the limbs, of what use are the eyes?
ai.translation: If one's eyes cannot perceive the inner thoughts of another from their outward signs, of what use are those eyes among the limbs of the body?
ai.modern: ஒருவருடைய முகக்குறிப்பைக் கொண்டு அவருடைய மனக்குறிப்பை உணர்ந்துகொள்ள முடியாவிட்டால், உடலின் உறுப்புகளுள் கண்களால் என்ன பயன் விளையும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the true purpose of sight in social and intellectual life. The word 'kuṟippu' is used in two senses here: first as the outward physical sign or expression, and second as the inward intention or feeling. The poet argues that the eyes are not merely for seeing physical objects, but for reading the unspoken thoughts of others. If a person's eyes lack this deeper perception and empathy, they are useless ornaments that serve no greater purpose than any other limb.

ai.literal: Like a crystal that shows that which is near, the face will show that which is intensely felt in the mind.
ai.translation: Just as a crystal reflects whatever is placed near it, the face reveals what is intensely felt within the mind.
ai.modern: அருகில் உள்ள பொருளைக் காட்டும் பளிங்கைப் போல, மனதில் உள்ளதை முகம் காட்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to explain how the face acts as a mirror to the mind. The word 'பளிங்கு' refers to a clear crystal, which has no color of its own but instantly reflects the color and form of whatever object is placed next to it. Similarly, the human face immediately reveals whatever intense emotion or thought arises in the mind. A skilled observer can therefore read a person's inner thoughts and feelings simply by looking at their face.

ai.literal: Than the face, a more highly intelligent thing is there? Whether rejoicing or being angry, it itself will express beforehand.
ai.translation: Is there anything more highly intelligent than the face? Whether one is pleased or angry, the face itself anticipates and expresses it first.
ai.modern: முகத்தை விட அறிவுமிக்கது வேறு ஏதேனும் உண்டா? ஒருவன் மகிழ்ந்தாலும் அல்லது கோபித்தாலும், அவனது முகம் அவனுக்கு முன்பாகவே அதனை வெளிப்படுத்திவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet praises the face as the ultimate, instantaneous mirror of the human mind. The poet rhetorically asks if there is anything more intelligent ('முதுக்குறைந்தது') than the face. This is because whether a person feels joy ('உவப்பினும்') or anger ('காயினும்'), the face itself immediately anticipates ('முந்துறும்') and reveals those inner emotions before the person can even speak or consciously act.

ai.literal: If one obtains those who, looking into the mind, understand what has occurred, it is sufficient to stand looking at their face.
ai.translation: If one can find companions who can look into the mind and perceive what has occurred within, it is enough to merely stand looking at their face.
ai.modern: மனதைப் பார்த்து உள்ளே நிகழ்ந்ததை உணர்ந்து கொள்ளும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களைப் பெற்றால், அவர்கள் முகத்தைப் பார்த்துக்கொண்டு சும்மா நின்றாலே போதுமானது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the extraordinary value of having companions or advisors who can read minds. If a person is fortunate enough to find those who can look into the mind ('அகம் நோக்கி') and instantly understand what is felt or what has happened ('உற்றது உணர்வார்'), then spoken words become unnecessary. Simply standing before them and looking at their face ('முகம் நோக்கி நிற்க') is completely sufficient ('அமையும்') to communicate. The poet beautifully contrasts the deep inner perception of the wise with the effortless outer presence required of the seeker.

ai.literal: Both enmity and friendship the eye will reveal, if one finds those who understand the variations of the eye.
ai.translation: Both enmity and friendship will be revealed by the eyes, if one can find those who are skilled at reading the varying expressions of the eye.
ai.modern: கண்ணின் வேறுபட்ட குறிப்புகளைப் புரிந்து கொள்ளக்கூடியவர்களைப் பெற்றால், ஒருவருடைய பகைமையையும் நட்பையும் அவருடைய கண்களே காட்டிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how the eyes serve as a powerful medium of unspoken communication. It asserts that both hostility (பகைமை) and friendship (கேண்மை) are clearly expressed through a person's eyes. However, this silent message can only be understood if one finds observers who are capable of reading the subtle variations (வகைமை) in eye expressions. The eyes act as a mirror to the inner mind, but they require a perceptive reader to decode their true meaning.

ai.literal: Those who say 'we are of subtle understanding', when examining their measuring rod, other than the eye, there is nothing else.
ai.translation: For those who claim to possess subtle understanding, when you look for the instrument with which they measure others' minds, there is no other measuring rod than their own eyes.
ai.modern: நாங்கள் நுட்பமான அறிவுடையவர்கள் என்று சொல்லிக்கொள்பவர்கள், பிறருடைய மனக்கருத்தை அளந்து அறிவதற்குப் பயன்படுத்தும் அளவுகோலை ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அது அவர்களுடைய கண்ணே தவிர வேறு ஒன்றும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how highly perceptive people read the minds of others. Those who boast of having a sharp, subtle intellect (நுண்ணியம் என்பார்) must have a tool to gauge what is hidden in another person's heart. When we look closely to find what this measuring rod (அளக்குங்கோல்) is, we realize it is nothing other than their own eyes (கண் அல்லது இல்லை பிற). The eye acts as the ultimate instrument of perception, catching the unspoken thoughts and feelings of others instantly.
